Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: A person has told me that chemotherapy and radiotherapy are toxic and deadly, that they can give me a cure for my cancer through natural medicine. Is he right?
Answer: The herbal treatment. I know of at least two people who tried it (instead of classical cancer therapies), and they are the exact two people who vanished in the most painful way. One was a patient of my girlfriend. A young man with a peeing problem that turned out to be a prostate thing. He wanted to have many more girlfriends libido-wise, he wanted to perform, he did NOT want to wear diapers, he wanted to be erected, he wanted to be a man (in his own language). And he declined. He declined every single therapy (prostatectomy, psychiatric evaluation and help, hormone treatment) because his brother would prepare herbal emulsions and the like to cure him. And surprise, surprise — he turned into pieces under the supervision of his loving brother who did not know squat. The second subject is an actress called Sylvia Millecam.[1] A Dutch icon know for her uncanny talent to improvise, fast intuition and beauty. But Sylvia also had an uncanny obsession for (her own) beauty, and she would do anything to keep it that way. A mastectomy ? — no thanks (‘they” define me as an actress). Chemotherapy ? — how will I look afterwards ? So Sylvia, as an avid supporter of alternative medicine, chose to follow a guru who claimed to cure cancer and every single other disease known to mankind through her own radiating radiation into water (usually recorded months in advance) and through radio talk (also usually recorded months in advance), and her guru urged her to stop having classical medical treatments, and drink her radiated water, and listen to her radiated words instead. At a not-so-small cost, as you might have expected. And Sylvia died before she reached the age of 45 — the tumor had ruined her body as if a bomb had exploded.[2] She was a mere skeleton. She was a mere copy of a thought. She was someone who could have been saved, but who believed the herbal woman with that very big fee. These are some of the few people I have known who tried the natural course. And who were obliterated on the way. SOURCES: Dissection of the female abdomen, showing the kidneys, gravid (?) uterus, ovaries and fallopian tubes, with the arteries and blood vessels indicated in red. Colored lithograph by J. Roux, 1822. Wellcome Collection.

Question: Why do people with Alzheimer’s disease lose their ability to walk properly and become incontinent?
Answer: Alzheimer’s usually starts with forgetting small things (such as paying bills), but once the forgetting gets worse and beyond worse, more and more fundamental aspects of the patient’s life are “un-apped,” as if they never mastered them in the first place. That’s Alzheimer’s in a nutshell. Alzheimer patients live the inverse life of babies, and lose every learned and instinctive ability they ever had until they become empty people — sad hollow creatures without content, and without the ability to add content. Completely erased — Totally un-apped. SOURCES: Google images.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the most terrible thing you've heard of that happened to your child?
Answer: This happened to a friend of ours (and it happened to her child). She had noticed one early morning that some hair was wrapped around one of the fingers of her baby boy. It’s called a “hair tourniquet”: human hair (or some other type of thread) tied around a finger, toe, or male genital — usually this happens to very young children during the night. And usually things turn out all right, but as the term “tourniquet” suggests, the affected digit cannot receive an adequate blood supply, nor can blood be drained through the veins. So it can go wrong — in rare cases the digit even has to be amputated. In the case of our friend’s baby, his little finger top looked so badly swollen and discolored that she immediately tried to free the finger. And she succeeded in unwrapping it, but not much later her baby started to convulse, and went into cardiac arrest. When the paramedics arrived, there was nothing they could do. By removing the hair tourniquet, most probably a blood clot from the finger top was released into his little body, and caused severe thrombosis in the end. (A fatal sepsis caused by gangrene in his finger was an alternative possibility, but less likely.) The only thing she wanted to do was helping her baby as fast as she could. And she killed him instead. SOURCES: James Heilman, MD, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Have you ever read something about yourself in your own medical notes that shocked you?
Answer: My mother-in-law is a retired radiologist, and some time ago she told us a jaw-dropping experience which happened to her when she was still an active practitioner. She had a patient with severe pain in one of his collarbones, and so he needed a series of medical images to be taken. When my mother-in-law was making the images, she slipped and made images of one of the patient’s lungs instead of his collarbones. Many radiologists throw flawed images in the bin (so to speak) before even looking at them, but she took an accidental peep at one of the images, and immediately noticed a large dark mass in the patient’s lung. The patient had lung cancer and di not have the slightest clue !! So her report of the patient’s images came as a very big (and extremely shocking) surprise: “The patient has arthritis in one of his collarbones, and has a large cancerous tumor in his right lung.” Fortunately, the cancer hadn’t spread yet and after the appropriate therapies the patient was declared to be in complete remission. Without the accidental peek, the cancer most probably would have spread without being noticed, so after the shock came redemption. And in the end, the radiologist’s slip saved the day. SOURCES: Volume Rendering of a contrast enhanced abdominal CT scan. Rendering done with a Carestream workstation. (Through Google images.)

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the most savage revenge you've seen someone take on their ex?
Answer: We needed to meet at our notary’s office to sign the most horrible documents I ever had to sign. Documents that legally said we would not see each other anymore till the end of time. Documents that said that “we” was a dead word now. That “we” were gone. And we were. And when we were sitting in the small room — my guess is notaries always let ex-lovers wait in the very same room to let them feel how sad the decision is they are about to take — we could only talk about ridiculous stuff. (How is your new house ? Great. My life is so much better now.) But she was sitting there, only months in an after life which I still could not comprehend. And I hated it. My only revenge was that I was still alive — probably this is the worst answer of all time — but for me, showing her that I was still here, that I would stop giving in, that I would stop her from scarring me, that I would stop her from spreading lies (this was a difficult one, as you can imagine), She had a new husband now, a new house, and soon she would become pregnant and have new children, and nothing in my own being would ever be existent in that new life. And I knew that — sensed that, until my stomach hurt — and I was just sitting there, looking beautiful (I really was), while I saw my current life becoming my past. But we signed the documents. And that was that. SOURCES: the painting is my own.

Question: How do I tactfully tell someone that they smell bad?
Answer: “I could eat that girl for lunch — yeah, she dances on my tongue, tastes like she might be the one, and I could never get enough.” Some people definitely have a problem, and it is not impossible to narrow it down. The problem either is psychological — depression, or some problem related to dementia such as early-onset Alzheimer’s or Korsakov syndrome — or she has a drug addiction (pills, alcohol, powder), or she is a pervert. I’ve heard from my spouse (who is a urologist) what happens down there when people do not wash for a long time. (The smegma, anal hair shit balls, navel stones — the smell.) And I know love conquers many things, but does it conquer smell ? (Or anal hair shit balls.) Somebody who really smells should see a general practitioner — and in some cases: a psychiatrist — as soon as possible, to get her or him out of this mess. So you should tell him or her, and help. (And if you are having her for lunch, you should make an appointment too.) SOURCES: Google images.

Question: What is more dangerous, chemo therapy or cancer?
Answer: In my girlfriend’s ward, a young patient was diagnosed with prostate cancer in an early stage, with very good chances to fight and overcome it. But he needed a partial prostatectomy (partial removal of his prostate), and that made him hesitate. Because this patient was young, and he feared the possible consequences such as erectile dysfunction and urinary incontinence. His brother consequently convinced him to skip any medical therapy whatsoever, and proposed to prepare some herbal mixtures himself to cure his cancer. Not chemo — just herbs. So the boy did just that — not turning up when the surgery was scheduled, and drinking his brother’s juices. (No pun intended.) In the months that followed, he encountered more and more symptoms, and so he visited the urology ward again, only to decline any therapy not much later (his brother, you know). And then he re-appeared one final time. This time, with metastasis. And this time, a prostatectomy would not help him anymore. But in his specific case, chemo (combined with hormone treatment) would still give him an almost 100% chance to be alive in 5 years. But as I already wrote, this was his final visit. He was obliterated by his own choices (and his brother’s uncanny stupidity) within months. What is more dangerous, chemo therapy or cancer ? Guess. SOURCES: K. D. Schroeder, CC BY-SA 3.0 <Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported>, via Wikimedia Commons.

Question: As a doctor or nurse, have you ever encountered a patient who was too gross to touch?
Answer: This patient had prostate cancer, but his urologist refused to see him anymore and always found new excuses to postpone appointment. In the meanwhile, the cancer was growing inside. The patient knew he smelled really bad since a while, but he had no idea why. And since he was also in an incredible (and almost not bearable) amount of pain — a fact which was simply ignored by his urologist — he needed to change doctors. Fast. So he asked to see another urologist in another hospital (in the same hospital, he know it would not happen), and the day was finally there. Because something was protruding from his rectum, he was seen by a general surgeon first (probably because they were thinking about some type of prolapse, or hemorrhoids), but after a brief investigation, the surgeon called the new urologist who was scheduled to see him about his cancer. “You REALLY have to see this !” And yes, the surgeon and new urologist had noticed the horrible putrid smell right away, but they didn’t back down. And then the surgeon put her index finger against the patient’s rectum — which was superficially sedated, by the way — and an incredibly stinking fluid spurted with great force out of his rectum, right into the face of the urologist. And that was the cause of his external (and internal) stench — pus, loads and loads of pus. When they examined the patient in greater depth, it turned that the pus originated from the original prostate tumor, which — through the procrastination of the worst urologist in the world — had grown so big that most of the patient’s abdominal cavity was filled with tumor, and hence filled with pus as well. This man was a walking and talking pus ball, and he needed help right away. And that’s exactly what he got. Question: Have you ever thought your child was faking being sick, but later discovered it was something serious?
Answer: One year ago, the then 6-year-old daughter of a friend started to feel sick. She could not stop vomiting, but her mom — who is an anesthesiologist — did not feel the need to go the hospital (it’s a typical thing that some specialists do 🙄). She thought it was a mild case of stomach flu. But then her daughter said something which immediately made alarm bells ring (very loudly) in her head: “Mommy, I see two copies of you.” She took her daughter in her arms, and rushed to the ER. In the hospital, neurologists talked to the girl with suggestive questions to narrow down her condition, and although she could answer every single one of these questions, she almost felt asleep in between questions. And that was weird. And extremely worrying. Not having clue as to what was happening, samples of fluid near the little girl’s spinal cord were taken to exclude meningitis and encephalitis — both very dangerous options — but instead of the expected high blood cell count, the fluid turned out to be bloody. And that was even worse. A subsequent MRI showed an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in her little brain — a rare tangle of blood vessels that connects arteries and veins in the brain. A tangle of canned worms that shouldn’t be there.And the tangle was bleeding inside her head. The doctors decided to send her to a specialized unit in a nearby academic hospital, where she was treated, and she eventually survived the episode (after a long and tedious stay in the hospital). She was bleeding out to within an inch of her life, but she made it. This time, that is. Because unless she undergoes (micro) surgery, endovascular embolization or radio surgery to eliminate the tangle of canned worms in her head, the little girl walks around with a silently ticking time bomb upstairs. Ready to strike one final time. SOURCES: the image shows a woman after having surgery to remove a cavernoma — a related abnormal growth of vessels in the brain.[1]

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What are some amazing facts related to Google?
Answer: Don’t we all HATE Math, and aren’t we so proud of that ? As a mathematician, it is the most shameful thing I have to endure time and again when someone asks me about my work, and I answer that I’m a mathematician — “Oh, I was REALLY BAD at Math in high school. I HATED it.” So many people are so proud of their incompetence (but we knew that already). Sergey Brin and Larry Page weren’t though. And when so many people were so proud of their own mathematical illiteracy, Brin and Page wrote up a nice little high school linear algebra paper about eigenvalues (the horror !) and the like, which led to an extremely efficient way of defining a new search engine. Google, baby. These guys paid a lot of attention to the Math they learned in high school, instead of being so proud of not understanding it, disliking it, and openly detesting it — in a world in which most people see Math as a dead entity which bothers them more than anything else, two young beat the odds and turned Math (yet again) into an uncannily powerful device. The rest is history, as they say. SOURCES: image found through Google images (what else).[1]

Question: I found out my 6-year-old daughter isn’t biologically mine. What should I do? Should I continue raising her?
Answer: My girlfriend (who is a urologist) had a patient who found out he had a rare congenital disease in the weirdest of ways. His wife pushed him to go for a fourth kid, but she could not get pregnant. So she had him tested. And the semen sample revealed that he was born with a condition which disabled him to have babies from the very start. He had NO biological children on his own, as it turned out. But his wife still found a way to be impregnated on three separate occasions — a harlot hattrick, if you want — behind her husband’s back. So what did he do ? The answer is pretty simple — Since he deeply loved his three children, he continued raising, and loving them. But he ditched the wife 🙂 SOURCES: image taken from GIFer.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: I'm 61 years old and can't find anyone to be with me. What's wrong with me? Is there anything wrong if I'm doing something wrong to meet someone?
Answer: We spent the weekend in one of our favorite hotels, and on the first morning, we noticed a middle-aged lady sitting alone at breakfast, accompanied by her dog. He had a little harness on with his name on it, and her telephone number. The lady had seen that we were looking at her dog, and she started talking to us spontaneously. “His name is Sam. I always wanted to be a mother — it was my life dream — but I am 45 now, and figure that I will never be a mother now. So I bought a dog, and called him “Sam.” That’s how I would have called my daughter.” In three sentences, she expressed so much sorrow that we did not know what to say. She seemed like an extremely sad and lonely woman, and I don’t think there was anything wrong with her. Bad luck sometimes floats around. (And it has to land on somebody.) SOURCES: painting by Beksiński.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: As a nurse, has a patient ever demanded something completely unreasonable of you?
Answer: The old farmer only had one testicle left due to testicle cancer, and his remaining testicle had taken a hard hit from his favorite cow. The ball looked like a balloon. A very painful balloon. After a medical investigation, and before the urologist could even say what the verdict was, the patient stated the decision he had made, after a long and deep contemplation: “I am seventy-plus years old, and my wife an I do not share the bed anymore. We don’t need to spend extra energy nor money to save it. Just take it away, and I will be just fine.” That’s what he would do if one of his animals had one balloon ball left — amputate the entire scrotum, and that’s that. So the lady doctor should do the same thing, with a rubber band for that matter. (He would be fine.) My girlfriend tried to explain that he needed the testosterone in order to function as a man (hoping that he would understand this language). But the farmer refused to take it in because in his eyes, a testicle was a tool to procreate. (“So why not cut it off ?”) It took forever to explain that without testicles he would suffer from fatigue, hot flashes, muscle loss, poor facial hair growth and what have you. That on many levels he would turn into a woman in menopause, and that lifelong hormone treatment would be necessary to counterbalance the effects. And that he would become an extremely emotional farmer for no reason if he would ignore that very important treatment (which he would). In the end, he gave in though — and the testicle lived. But the dream remained. SOURCES: Dissections of the male genitals, upper thighs and pelvic region: two figures, with the arteries, blood vessels and veins indicated in red and blue. Colored lithograph by J. Roux, 1822. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Is there anyone who has a heart on the right side?
Answer: Absolutely ! Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal position. It only occurs in one in ten thousand people. Most probably the most famous person alive with Situs inversus is Enrique Iglesias, who was diagnosed very late in life with the fact that some of his visceral organs (including his heart) are mirrored from their normal position.[1] In 2023 Iglesias — who was 48 at the time — suffered from some health problems (possible of a cardio-vascular nature) which turned out to be caused by Situs inversus.[2] I am not sure how long he knew about his condition, but usually this is noted after a routine check-up at the General Practitioner’s, since a standard listening-to-the-heart check should reveal that something is not beating at the left side of the patient. And then, a mirror runs through it. SOURCES: the footnoted sites. For the image of Enrique Iglesias, I consulted Biography.com.[3] The medical image (of a case of Situs inversus) was taken from Cureus.[4]

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the saddest thing someone has said to an anesthesiologist before undergoing major surgery?
Answer: A young woman in her early twenties with a kidney tumor. (An extremely rare case from the start.) The tumor has already spread to the lymph nodes, and both the kidney and positive lymph nodes have to be removed. And they are. But not much later, she is back in the hospital with new symptoms, and the cancer is again in the lymph nodes. She needs a second operation but now the situation is even worse — the cancerous lymph nodes mass is very close to the vena cava (a large vein which carries blood to the heart from other parts of the body), and if it grows some more, it will enter the wall of the vena cava. And that will be the end of it. The urologist who will perform the surgery knows this, and she also knows that the patient has just become a mother, with a baby of six months old. Before she goes asleep, she looks the anesthesiologist and urologist deep in the eyes, and asks whether this is her last chance to see her baby become a toddler. And the silence answers her question more than any words can. Less than two months later, she is in the hospital again. The cancer has grown into her vena cava, and she has only a couple of weeks left. And when she hears the news — which she, as a young, very intelligent and independent woman, had expected but tried to ignore the best she could — she starts crying, crying, crying. And only one sentence vibrates through her trembling heart as her world shuts down — Her baby is eight months old. Her baby is eight months old. SOURCES: Head, neck, shoulder and chest of a dissected male écorché, with arteries and blood vessels indicated in red. Colored lithograph by J. Roux, 1822. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: If XY is automatically male as some people claim then should an XY person be allowed in women's spaces?
Answer: Not at all. Take Jamie Lee Curtis. She was born with XY chromosomes (which means she is “karyotypically male”), but she was born with Testicular Feminization Syndrome (TFS) (also called Androgyn Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS)):[1] This is precisely the effect in testicular feminization syndrome -- there are internal, undescended testes and no uterus, fallopian tubes, or ovaries, but externally the labia, vagina, and clitoris all develop. Typically, the labia and clitoris are indistinguishable from those of a normal (46, XX) female, but the vagina is shorter than usual or sometimes absent. Breast development is that of a normal woman, and many other sexual characteristics of body habitus, such as pelvic shape are also normal. Armpit and pubic hair on the other hand is decreased or absent. And very importantly: patients with TFS cannot have children. And yes: Jamie has children, but they are adopted. Her father has addressed “her secret” a number of times in public, and at one point in her life, she had an undescended testicle removed. Her AIS case is actually well known in the medical world, and serves as an example at several medical grad schools in the US. Big deal. Still, she looks like a woman to me. SOURCES: the footnoted site. For the photograph: Jamie Lee Curtis at the 1980 Canned festival.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: As an attorney, have you ever experienced a case that made you re-evaluate your life?
Answer: Two years ago, a befriended attorney told me during a wedding dinner that the hardest cases he dealt with were the child abusers — some of them had even killed an underaged child (after or during the abuse). He had children of his own, by the way. Another friend of ours (she was an MD, of all people) shouted: “They should KILL all of them !” My friend-attorney did not agree. He kindly told her that everyone has the right to be defended, whatever dark deed they had done. Our friend did not agree. (“They should be TORTURED as well !!”) He proceeded with explaining that almost 80% of child abusers had been abused themselves as a kid, and that although they had turned out to become assailants (and even murderers), they also had been victims, and still were. Most of them hated themselves for what they had done (knowing how traumatizing it was). The other 20% consisted of sick people — psychologically so twisted that every day was a fight against demons they did not understand (and most often they lost). Talking to his clients had totally changed his perspective on these people — people who had committed violent and depraved crimes, who had taken someone’s innocence for good, people who had even killed. But above all, even they were human beings. (“He had never met a monster, after all these years.”) Our MD friend did not even listen anymore, and shouted that every single child abuser should be castrated (she assumed they were all men, which they aren’t), and then hanged. She lived in a black-and-white world, though. He did not. SOURCES: for the image, I consulted Tales of Times Forgotten.[1]

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What surprised you when your husband died?
Answer: What surprised me the most when my ex-wife died, was the letter. I found it in the mailbox a couple of weeks after she had passed away (she had died from late stage breast cancer and her demise was awful), and I could barely believe what it said. Because what it said was that I was an official widower now — although we had been divorced for more than ten years ! — and as my ex-wife had been a high school teacher, I now “had the right to receive a monthly widower pension from the state.” (When I read those words, I could not stop myself from wondering whether she had known this fact in the months, weeks and days before she died, while finishing up the necessary paperwork.) The very idea that I was somehow involved in the aftermath of her death was almost spooky. And since I found the whole idea utterly perverse, I refused the pension. No blood money for me. SOURCES: painting by Beksiński.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Why is silence the best revenge?
Answer: The final time I ever spoke to her was in the office of our then-notary, to put our final signatures on a document which would finalize our divorce, and make me the new, single owner of our house. It was one of the most important days of my life. The damage was already done, and every single trace of “we” had been demolished through a period of cheating and lying — I knew that. But still: seeing her again for the first time after she had admitted what she had done was really big. She was now living with the douchebag. And we had only talked on the phone about money, differences, our house, and all that was lost. After ten years of being together, after ten years of sharing, talking, moving, laughing, sitting, loving, denying and, in the end, hating, we sat together again, waiting for the secretary when it was our time to meet the notary. We were the only clients in the room, and did not know what to say. (I remember I was so surprised to see how small her head was. Anyways.) She was extremely surprised by the fact that I looked really good — she had hoped that the utter misery she had tried to burry me in would destroy me, and would turn me into a weak adversary in the battle about money, and our house. Money had become so important to her (and I was so appalled). But even then, I was very relaxed and showed my best smile to hide my loss. And she had a very hard time to cope with my safety smile — almost cried in the act. She never understood what kept me alive in the end (and she would never know). What is the best revenge against your ex who emotionally destroyed you ? I have to admit that the water had become really deep — even for me — and that the waves tried to bring me down, that the space below my feet (which felt so cold) was way too deep. But I kept my head above the water. And never stopped swimming. SOURCES: Francisco Goya, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: As a patient, what is the most distasteful thing a doctor ever said to you?
Answer: A befriended urologist told us at a wedding party that he performed digital vaginal examinations on every single one of his female patients when they visit him for a medical consultation. Only those who are (often very) young, by the way. There is no medical indication whatsoever to do this with (or better: to) a healthy teenager who has been experiencing peeing problems, or a kidney stone. But he does it anyway. So to be totally clear: this is a man who uses his MD status to digitally abuse his patients, telling them that this is part of a routine medical investigation, knowing all too well that his teenage patients won’t suspect him of what he is actually doing because he is a urologist after all. And then he proceeds with his ever so helping hand. SOURCES: Graves, William Phillips, 1870-1933, No restrictions, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: How does a rescuer deal with a person who has been cut in half by a truck and obviously will not survive, but is still alive?
Answer: This patient — although unknown — became a part of my life, if only for a short while. His legs had been removed, his penis and most of the tissue surrounding it (think lymph nodes, scrotum, and then think more), but the cancer was eating him inside out (part 2) at a faster rate, and more refined methods were needed to keep him alive. So they sliced his body, 1/5th of an inch at a time. Every single day. At some point — near his stomach, when most everything of what a normal life could still have defined had declined opposition — the MDs decided that the salami method had to be stopped. Almost nothing of this kind man was left, and enough was enough. He had not been cut in half by a truck — this truck had been very patient — and although he was now half the man he used to be, he asked the doctors to stop, and to let him go as the tiny (but still so very tall) man he had become. And his urologist — who had been with him all the way — cried tears while holding this tiny man in her arms, as his final seconds ticked away. Even without his legs, he was taller than most of us. SOURCES: The circulatory system: dissection of the abdomen and pelvic region of a man, side view, showing the intestines and bladder, with the arteries indicated in red. A surgical instrument is shown below. Colored lithograph by J. Maclise, 1841/1844. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Why is age 70 considered old age?
Answer: Let’s have a look at the cancerous side of your question. It is estimated that a child born today has a 1 in 2 chance of developing cancer at some point in its life, and this percentage is on the rise.[1] It is extremely important to note that this estimate does not take into account that not all cancers are diagnosed before someone dies, and that this estimate only applies to developed countries. In underdeveloped countries, many people are never diagnosed because there aren’t enough hospitals and doctors to witness what is really medically going on with the population. And, on the other hand, in those countries the inhabitants die young. (In Chad, for instance, the average person dies at 53.)[2] The essential reason for the 1-in-2 estimate in developed countries is the simple fact that children who are born today will become very old on average, and on the cancer ladder this translates in the fact that relatively many of them will get cancer at some point. It’s one of the many compensations for getting old, but certainly one of the most striking ones. And needless to say, this cancerous formalism applies to many other conditions as well. It’s Nature’s way of telling us that we are getting old — too old — and this clearly translates in the ever growing medical costs our modern developed societies have due to this very fact. We get too old, so we cost more and more. And alas, this profoundly applies to you a 70-year-old. If you do not have cancer as a 70-year-old, or if you were not diagnosed yet, then be sure that your chances are growing every day, until there’s that cough that does not go away, the typical armpit lump, hoarse voice, back pain, or that innocent but ever returning diarrhea. Because it’s the big C that is hiding underneath — And it’s coming for you. SOURCES: the footnoted sites. For the image: painting by Nicola Samori.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: After providing a terminal diagnosis to a patient, what is the most profound strength of character you witnessed?
Answer: A seventy-five-year-old patient entered the ER with severe pain in the groin. He was also experiencing a fever, and in general his condition was deteriorating fast. My girlfriend (a urologist) had never seen it on an actual patient, but she had learned about it as a student, and a routine medical examination confirmed her first impression. Fournier’s gangrene. An acute necrotic infection of the penis, scrotum or perineum, which is essentially a flesh-eating disease (necrotizing fasciitis in fancy medical words), with a very high mortality rate. Only 1/62,500 males (and some females, for that matter) get it, but the diagnosis is always bad news.[1] In this case, it was a death sentence. In an ultimate try to save the patient, she tried to remove as much dead tissue of the infected area as possible during improvised surgery — and that included the complete removal of the patient’s penis. But the gangrene kept spreading at an absolutely devastating rate, and soon it became clear that this patient’s case was beyond medical control. When the old man awoke, my girlfriend explained that he had not much time left. That the gangrene was eating him at an unsettling rate, and that he only had a couple of hours left “at best.” It was a though message to bring, and she was almost in tears when she broke the news. The man gently smiled at my girlfriend, and said: “Thank you, doctor. I am completely ready to go, and I am glad the agony is almost over.” And not much later, it was. SOURCES: the footnoted site. Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What do doctors really think of their morbidly obese patients?
Answer: Morbidly obese patients often do not realize that ERs and ORs simply do not have the personnel or devices to lift them and turn them over. When an emergency procedure is planned, this very obstruction could mean the difference between life and death. Even in common procedures complications can occur due to severe overweight. Some time ago, my girlfriend had a morbidly obese patient who had a kidney stone, and the kidney stone would be removed through a so-called lithotripsy — a non-invasive procedure in which focused ultrasonic energy or shock waves are sent directly to the stone, so that the shock waves break it into smaller stones that will eventually pass through the urinary system. The fat layer of this patient — who happened to be a good friend — was just too thick for the shock waves to travel through, and the surgery did not work out in the end. One other time, an invasive surgery on a morbidly obese patient had to be stopped because the nurses could not lift a huge bag of fat which was obstructing the affected area. This happens all the time, by the way. (And let’s not even start about the morbidly obese patients who immediately start talking about “body shaming” if they are told they need to lose weight due to urgent health issues.) What do doctors really think of their morbidly obese patients ? In the case of surgeons, they really dread morbidly obese patients because it’s often impossible to offer the required medical help, or perform the necessary surgical procedures. And that’s not what a doctor wants. SOURCES: Google images.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Is it okay when I, as a woman, go with my 4-year-old son to the men’s bathroom?
Answer: Of course it is. If a child has to go, it has to go. It’s a mystery to me why almost all answers to this question forbiddingly say “no.” I am a father, and I have a daughter, and when she was younger and she really had to go, I went to the women’s bathroom if that was a choice, and the men’s wasn’t. (She is eleven now and I would do the same thing if the call was urgent.) I did that a number of times myself by the way, if nature asked for an intervention that could not wait. And I would do it anytime soon again if nature started calling again. If we need to go, we need to go. Nobody in the men’s room would give you a hard time because your toddler girl needs to pee, or go for No. 2 — they all understand the urgency. I am just so shocked that for many women (who answered this question) this seems to be a big problem. Am I missing something ? (Or are they ?) SOURCES: "Unfinished cartoon for a Madonna and Child" (1525-30) by Michelangelo Buonarroti. Black and red chalk, white gouache, brush and brown wash. Casa Buonarroti, Florence.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What was your weirdest moment as a nurse?
Answer: This 50-something-year-old patient suffered from young-onset dementia, and had broken a hip. He had to stay in bed until the operation, but he needed extra surveillance because of his other condition — the man forgot most everything, including what had happened to him only an hour ago. So not long after his ER entrance, he asked a nurse what he was doing in the hospital — “There is NOTHING wrong with me !” The nurse explained that he had broken a hip, and that he should lie really still until he could go to the OR and have an operation. But the patient did not believe her, as he had no recollection of an accident nor of pain, since “he had NOT broken his hip, and would leave this please ASAP !!” But he had. And less than a second later, he jumped off the bed. SOURCES: KaplanMDlv, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.[1]

Question: What horrible thing you read today shocked you?
Answer: The news that Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone (again) ran a world record on the 400 meters hurdles on the USA Olympic trials. Her great rival Femke Bol, asked it aloud only a couple of weeks ago — Why didn’t Sydney McLaughlin enter an international competition in more than one year ? Why does she so rarely compete ? Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Why does Björk look Asian?
Answer: You are most probably referring to her slanted eyes — the so-called “epicanthic fold.” My guess is that Björk — Icelandic for “birch” by the way — has some Sámi (Lapp) ancestry, and (a part of) this indigenous people from the larger Sápmi region (comprising Northern parts of Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia) is well known to display the epicanthic fold. It’s a thing of beauty — And not only Asian. SOURCES: photograph found through Google images.[1]

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Has a patient ever said something that sent a chill down your spine?
Answer: The Egyptian woman wanted her husband tested ASAP because they could not get pregnant, and getting pregnant was a necessity for her. So he turned in a semen sample, and the semen sample was checked out. And when their urologist read the results she was deeply surprised, for this sample contained not one single living sperm cell at all. And after some further testing, it turned out that the husband was born with a congenital condition which made him infertile from the start. This man could not have babies — he never could. So why was the urologist so surprised ? The couple had three children, all born in Egypt. And the Egyptian husband was convinced that he was their biological dad, and now he was here, essentially childless with three children. And the whole scene chilled their urologist to the bones, because his wife kept on pushing for more answers, kept on pushing for miraculous solutions while she knew all too well that he was not the biological father of her three children (that man or those men lived in Egypt) — she kept on pushing, and pushing, and pushing, while her husband had been infertile the whole time (and he still did not know the truth). This was obviously a woman without scruples — This was a woman without a heart. SOURCES: GIF found through GIFER.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Have you ever had a bad gut feeling about someone and it was right?
Answer: I was waiting in a coffee shop for my order, when I noticed a women standing to my left-hand side, and the very sight of her really startled me. She also ordered something, but seemed to be distracted, as if she hardly noticed the other people in the room. She looked like a ghost — a shell with hardly anything left inside — and something was going on with her facial skin as well (as it was a dark shade of yellow and pitted like the peel of an orange). And for some reason, I was convinced that this woman was dying. I needed to do some work on my laptop, so I took a seat, and started working. The ghostly woman sat down as well, and her body language seem to confirm my gut feeling: she was looking at her cell phone but her eyes told me that no information was coming in. She was staring at something the other people in the coffee house could not see — something which was coming closer, and which was draining her every feeling. Something that made her desperate. Something very cold. Two months later, I received a text message from a friend. It said that my ex-wife had died. SOURCES: painting on the left-hand side by Stephen Early. The painting on the right-hand side was created by Mar Ko.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the biggest scam a door-to-door salesman ever tried to pull over on you?
Answer: It was a catholic priest. We had bought an old house in a new village, and the previous owner of the house was a devote god-fearing christian who had been very active in the local church community. So when we moved in, the local priest paid us a visit to talk about our beliefs, with the grand plan of wheeling us into the church community. And so one day our doorbell rang, and when we opened the door, he entered our house without even asking us if that was okay (it wasn’t), taking us young people for granted, as if he owned us in some moral way (he didn’t). And just like that, he started talking about “our future role in the local church community.” I quickly interrupted him, and explained that we were atheists, and that I had never believed in his and any other god for even one second in my entire life. And that his disrespectful way of talking to us strongly reminded me of the many reasons why we would NOT be a member of his congregation. He looked at me as if he had never met an atheist in his life (and maybe he hadn’t), and he was totally shocked that atheists could live in this very house where religion had been THE basic value for more than thirty years. Then he walked outside without saying another word and without a friendly goodbye — apparently, to people like us a note of friendliness was not needed. We were lost, after all. SOURCES: Leonardo da Vinci, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: When is depression considered severe?
Answer: When the depressed person is all smiles. One of our friends did just that. She had suffered from severe depressions over the years, and the roughest of all her episodes was shaking up her life (and that of her boyfriend, who also existed). Then, one day she suddenly was a shiny happy person, and most (but not all) of us thought she was doing really well again. In reality, she had bought a rope. She had planned a plan. She had chosen a day. And she was counting the minutes and the seconds till that day, and hid everything under shiny happy smiles. And when the day came, we found her, hanging. My dear aunt June did the exact same thing: “after” her very last depression, she started shining like a sunbeam. But she written long goodbye letters for her husband (my dear uncle), and her son. And she had bought sleeping pills, and she had chosen a day. She was counting the minutes and the seconds till that day, and hid everything under shiny happy smiles. She visited us one last time when our daughter was born. And then, one morning my dear uncle found her next to him in bed, cold and stiff. The letters were on the kitchen table. When is depression considered severe ? When your depressed loved one is suddenly all smiles. Because she or he has a plan. SOURCES: the painting (Iscariot No. 3) is mine.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: People with autism who got diagnosed (really) late, what was a dead giveaway you didn’t notice was autism related until you got diagnosed?
Answer: I know I should not do this, but I am doing it anyhow. There is not a single person (with autism) who can answer this question. Which means that any single person who answers this question as an autistic person, is actually not autistic. Let’s first translate the question into a more physical-medical context: “People who got in a wheelchair really late, can you please walk to me to explain when you noticed you could not walk ?” They can’t. Because they can’t walk. They can’t take a stroll because the legs don’t work. (“There was this car accident, you know.”) And autistic patients can’t either. If they suffer from REAL autistic spectrum disorder — with REAL, I mean that as a paraplegic, you don’t have any feeling in your legs so you can’t walk around with a stick — they cannot answer this question. Because real ASD patients do not understand that they have a disorder. The saddest Quora accounts are those which say (in the heading): I am autistic, and proud of it (2,300 answers). Patients — the REAL ones — with ASD do not understand that diagnosis. Do not write answers about their disorder, because the not-understanding is a part of the diagnosis. If you understand and write about it, you don’t have it — not really. If you are able to walk in one way or the other, you are not paraplegic. So, please-please-please, so-called autistic writers on Quora: I know you need attention, and I know you need a way to be special (for some reason). But this is not the way. It’s hard enough to not feel your legs. SOURCES: drawing by Beksiński.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Which celebrity (stars) had a secret that was finally revealed?
Answer: It was a birth defect, and so what. It was a bit messier when she was a child, but as she grew up, Jamie Lee Curtis turned into a marvelously looking person. Technically Jamie was born like a man, but medically she suffers from something called Testicular Feminization Syndrome (TFS) from birth:[1] This is precisely the effect in testicular feminization syndrome -- there are internal, undescended testes and no uterus, fallopian tubes, or ovaries, but externally the labia, vagina, and clitoris all develop. Typically, the labia and clitoris are indistinguishable from those of a normal (46, XX) female, but the vagina is shorter than usual or sometimes absent. Breast development is that of a normal woman, and so are many other sexual characteristics of body habitus, such as pelvic shape. On the other hand, armpit and pubic hair are markedly decreased or even absent. And very importantly: patients with TFS cannot have children. (And Jamie Lee has indeed stated on various occasions that she biologically cannot have kids.) Often, due to their more boyish looks, TFS patient can grow up to be more beautiful than “ordinary” woman, and Jamie is the pinnacle of this formalism. Personally, I do not care at all what her congenital disorder is, because she looks the way she looks, whatever defect is hiding deep inside. (Especially in the 1985 movie Perfect she/he really looked absolutely perfect to me. She never called though.) On the other hand, some people are really disturbed by the very fact that biologically Jamie Lee Curtis is not a woman, but who cares ? She looks like a woman, feels like a woman, and smells like a woman. And that’s about all it takes. SOURCES: the footnoted site. (For the photograph: Jamie Lee Curtis, gorgeous, at the 1980 Cannes festival.)

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the best lie you have ever told your child?
Answer: Not so long ago, I made a Lilac wand for my daughter (a magic wand made from Summer lilac wood), and gave it to her as a present. She was extremely excited, and as soon as we were back home, she tried to levitate herself. Subsequently, she was extremely disappointed — even cried — that it did not work, and I was totally surprised, but above all amazed that she really believed that the Lilac wand would pull her into the skies. They never do such a thing for the first time. But that’s just a matter of patience, of course. SOURCES: the photograph is my own.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Did you know there was something wrong with your health, but no one believed you, until one day you received a correct diagnosis?
Answer: This is a Christmas story. And it’s not my story, but the story of a young man who was helping his mom in the kitchen, preparing New Year’s Eve dinner. When at some point his mom dropped something on the floor, he was the first to bend down and pick it up. That was a typical Mark thing — helping all the time. But when he bent down, something snapped in his neck. A lump occurred on one side of his neck, but he had no pain, and felt fairly okay. (But still.) And it’s not that his family members did not believe him when he said that something in his neck had snapped — some even proposed to drive him to a hospital, just in case — rather, it was an inconvenience on New Year’s Eve, and it did not hurt so how bad could it be, right ? And as no one was insisting, he took his bike and rode to the hospital himself. By then, the lump had considerably grown, but nobody had noticed that (or maybe they ignored it altogether). They would never see him again. When Mark arrived, he collapsed near the entrance of the ER. And there was nothing the ER doctors and nurses could do for him, although they tried, and tried, and tried. Later, the medical doctors discovered that Mark had Syphilis — a fact which was (most probably) unknown to him — and that he had developed an arteriovenous malformation (an abnormal tangle of blood vessels) in his neck. As he bent over to help his mom, the tangle had snapped, and bled him to death within the hour. And ended Mark’s story, on New Year’s Eve. SOURCES: Tertiary syphilitic ulceration of the scalp, see page for author, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What has an actress refused and was controversial?
Answer: Jamie Lee Curtis always refused to address her medical condition — and this is perfectly okay — but she also never denied it. It was a birth defect, and so what. You see, technically she was born like a man, but medically she appears to have something called Testicular Feminization Syndrome (TFS) from birth:[1] This is precisely the effect in testicular feminization syndrome -- there are internal, undescended testes and no uterus, fallopian tubes, or ovaries, but externally the labia, vagina, and clitoris all develop. Typically, the labia and clitoris are indistinguishable from those of a normal (46, XX) female, but the vagina is shorter than usual or sometimes absent. Breast development is that of a normal woman, and so are many other sexual characteristics of body habitus, such as pelvic shape. Armpit and pubic hair are markedly decreased or absent. And very importantly: patients with TFS cannot have children. Personally, I do not care at all what her congenital disorder is, because I think she looks absolutely terrific — especially in the 1985 movie Perfect, in which she/he really looked perfect to me. But maybe you, dear gentle man and gall, are disturbed by me mentioning her/his early predicament, while it won’t change an iota of her almost perfect characteristics (and I know many of you agree). Is an X, or an Y, really that important here ? — You tell me. SOURCES: the footnoted site. (For the photograph: Jamie Lee Curtis at the 1980 Canned festival.)

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Have you been to a doctor and they can't find anything physically wrong with you, but you know something is wrong?
Answer: The patient was in a lot of pain, and so she called her urologist because the family practitioner attributed her pain to the kidney stone she had inside. But when she described her pain to the urologist, the latter knew right away that this was definitely NOT the kidney stone. Then, the patient said that “it was so painful that I had to ask my dad to drive really slowly.” And this simple symptom changed everything. The urologist immediately posed an awkward question: “Did it hurt more when the road was bumpy ?” It did. Bumps made the pain much more intensive. After applying pressure on a specific point on the right-hand side of the patient’s abdomen and then quickly releasing the pressure, the patient’s reaction said it all (she screamed). The problem was not urological. She had acute appendicitis, and needed emergency surgery only moments later. And despite the very big mistake of her general practitioner, she made it through the day — But only barely. SOURCES: Annals of Surgery, vol. 197, No. 5 (1983), pp. 495–506.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Do you think Lady Gaga's "it's not my fault if you brought your kids to my show" a valid deflection for parents who get offended by her saying or doing vulgar things in her live shows?
Answer: There’s this famous Swedish pop singer called Tove Lo — “Sweden’s darkest pop export” according to Rolling Stone[1] — and she always flashes her breast during a gig. Everyone who buys a ticket to see Tove Lo knows this. Everyone who buys a ticket to see Lady Gaga, knows essentially what Gaga does. (It’s not that shocking.) SOURCES: GIF taken from GIPHY (and the footnoted site).

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the saddest thing you've ever seen happen in a bar?
Answer: There was an old pub a few blocks away from the house where I lived, and I spent at least three evenings per week in that place. And so did Nicole and Mister Ebert. Nicole was a woman in her mid fifties who suffered from Turner’s syndrome, and therefore she had some characteristic physiological features (she was very short, had a webbed neck and a remarkable facial structure), and Mister Ebert — in his early sixties, retired and Jazz connoisseur — was her lover. They both were hardcore alcoholics, and subsequently they often had loud and almost physical drunken brawls about nothing. On other occasions they could be libidinous as well, and their sometimes shocking behavior often reminded me of old French paintings for some reason. They lived on their instincts, like demented people sometimes do. If Nicole was alone, she sometimes bothered people with drunken stories, to a point that she was thrown out and then banned for a couple of days. (On such evenings, she often could not pay for her drinks because she drank more than she could afford.) One day, I heard from the owner of the pub (whom I knew really well) that Mister Ebert had been hit by a car the other night. The driver jumped out of the car, took Mister Ebert’s wallet, jumped back in the car, and then ran over his head before he drove away. Mister Ebert’s head was crushed like a watermelon — locally, the road was covered with pieces of his skull and brain tissue, and teeth. In the days, weeks and months after the robbery, the pub became a lot quieter after Mister Ebert’s stellar demise. Nicole still frequented the pub, but the smiles were gone, and mostly she was drinking without much appetite, only searching for something to ease the pain. For more than a decade, she wandered down the streets near her little apartment close to the pub, talking to herself, and estranged from her surroundings. Looking for Mister Ebert, and all that jazz. SOURCES: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Au Moulin Rouge, 1892-1895, The Art Institute of Chicago, Helen Birch Bartlett Memorial Collection, 1928.610 (© The Art Institute of Chicago / DR).

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: As a doctor, have you ever diagnosed and saved yourself from a medical emergency?
Answer: One of the best friends of my mother-in-law (almost) did. She was a neurologist — notice the word “was” — and one day she became aware of the fact that she forgot words. Everyday words for everyday things, and she could not name them. She also turned more introvert and silent, as if it was hard for her to escape her own mind. As if she had been taken prisoner by something completely unknown to her. One day, there was a dinner party for my mother-in-law’s retirement, and Anita (the neurologist) was sitting at our table. And she did not say more than a couple of words, just basically staring without really seeing, totally absent, as if she was depressed without being depressed. Not much later, she scheduled a number of neurological and cognitive tests for herself, and ordered an MRI of the brain. And the MRI images revealed that she had a cancerous tumor in her brain the size of a mandarin orange. And that is where my answer unfortunately diverges from the other answers, because the mandarin orange could not be removed nor stopped. She was too late. Due to her own discovery, she lived longer than she would have if she had not noticed her own symptoms, but as the tumor grew, her stillness grew as well. Until nothing was left. SOURCES: Neck and face: dissection, with blood-vessels and nerves indicated in red and blue. Colored line engraving by W.H. Lizars, 1822/1826. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What ended your relationship with your best friend?
Answer: He wasn’t my best friend, but one of the best at the time. And he was cheating — boy was he cheating. He married too early with a pretty famous news anchor, but from the very beginning she kind of handled him like a whipping boy. They met each other through law studies, and he was the smartest of the two, but she was ruthless. In law, that can definitely make a difference. So he became a judge, and she became a reporter, and later news anchor. And she did not care. She did not care about his values, about his feelings about important choices they had to make about their kids (school, religion, books, love), about his (low-life, in her opinion) parents, about his friends, about life from his point of view. Did I mention she was very rich ? And one day she mentioned that she had cheated on him, but only “small time,” and only because he was so boring at times. And something cracked inside. And one day, not much later, he told me he was seeing someone from work — someone extremely exciting without prejudice, and without all the terrible noise his wife always was accompanied with — and he wanted to go for her. Only he didn’t. He kept texting me, sending me pictures, contacted me for yet another conversation about his lover, about how lovely she was, and then about how he could not leave his wife (with all the power and the money), and at some point I warned the whipping boy that he should stop contacting me, because I was in a divorce fight myself (cheating and all), and I had kind of stopped respecting him by now. So I said he had to tell his wife the truth, stop pretending to be the Shakespearean tormented lover, and finally open his mouth as the judge of his own life. But he didn’t. And kept on playing Shakespeare. And to make the drama even worse, I cryptically told his wife what was going on in a late night Facebook-chat-gone-wrong session, and that was basically the end of our friendship. One year ago — after nine years of silence — she has filed for divorce, and the judge has contacted me again. But from every single communication I received from his part, I hear one thing and one thing only. The whining of a man who thinks he is a victim, and who refuses to see his own serial denial (and later cheating) as even the slightest reason for feeling guilt or remorse. For he is still the whipping boy. (And I am not.) SOURCES: the painting is my own.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: My tenant pays rent on time, but his rent is very low than market rent. How can I get him out?
Answer: Ask my uncle Pitt (he is not related). He lived together with his father in a beautiful and very spacious 2,000 square feet apartment with a beautiful view on an adjacent park, in the center of a historical European city. When my grandfather almost died from bowel obstruction, he changed into a different man during his 11-months-stay in the hospital, and had to move to a nursing home. But my uncle stayed in his apartment, alone now. And he loved it. The (new) silence, the park, his plant collection in front of the huge glass windows at the sunny side of the apartment, his 18th century clock collection, the space, the center of the city at a walking distance — it was a dream. And then his landlord died. The landlord was an old man whom my grandfather had known well, and he never had a problem with the very low rent his favorite and very correct tenants had to pay him, because they liked each other, and because he did not need the money anyway. The new landlord was his daughter, and the new landlord was a landlord with money who, totally unlike her deceased father, wanted more money. Quantity of quality. More, more, more. So she tripled the rent as soon as her landlord father left the building. (How that must have hurt, dead for a couple of days and already betrayed.) And my uncle Pitt (not related) left his old home with a lot of pain — I helped him move, and the whole thing was very sad. And when the old apartment was finally empty, we left its silence behind and looked at it for one last time. And we saw my dead grandfather standing for a split second behind the huge glass windows — the sunny side. And then he was gone. SOURCES: painting by Odd Nerdrum (© Walker Art Center).

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: Why can't a person with Alzheimer's have a fact sheet in front of them reminding them of everything, including the fact that they have Alzheimer's, and that they’re expected to be constantly confused?
Answer: They often have such a sheet, but there is a twist. Take my friend Josy. When searching for a glass in one of her cupboards, one of her sons found a pile of bills. Unpaid bills — dozens of them. His mom had no idea what they were doing there. Not much later, she was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s, in a not-so-early stage. Still, they decided that she would stay home — alone ! — for as long as possible. And then her condition progressed over a period of about seven years. Three major things happened: Because of the 30 seconds rule, she needed sheets of paper with instructions, all prepared by her sons. (Turn out the stove. Turn out the kitchen light. Change your diaper. READ THE SHEETS.) And this worked rather well for a while, until the words on the sheets stopped making sense to her. They became meaningless strings of letters without a face, as if the words were hiding, and the letters stopped speaking. Her life shrunk into a world without words — Betrayed by the silence of letters. SOURCES: painting by Rhys Knight.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What are some things you should never do in an operating room?
Answer: The Ukrainian wife of a friend needed to have a hysterectomy. Her husband recommended his best friend (who happened to be an OB/GYN) to perform the procedure, and remove her uterus. This was the end of 2023. And that was what happened. After the procedure, she did not feel very well, and in the end she had to be opened up again by a befriended surgeon (instead of a urologist, whom he should have called). Her bladder had been severely ruptured by the OB/GYN, but the general surgeon could not fix it, so a urologist had to jump in to reconstruct the bladder. The Ukrainian lady became more sick in the days after the reconstruction, and eventually an emergency operation had to be scheduled to save her life because she was actually dying when the new procedure started (due to blood poisoning). Once opened up again (by the urologist and surgeon), it then turned out that besides butchering her bladder, the OB/GYN had also cut off one of her ureters. And so further reconstruction surgery was needed to finally end her misery. And she survived. But in the end, the one thing you do not do in the OR is letting an OB/GYN perform surgery on a patient — it’s a well-kept secret in hospitals that OB/GYNs mess up many patients, and it is also a well-kept secret that general surgeons and urologists are called in (on a shockingly regular basis) to save the day. The patients do not know this, of course. And they’re paying the price. SOURCES: Graves, William Phillips, 1870-1933, No restrictions, via Wikimedia Commons.

Name: Thomas Cayne
Question: What is the best way to get revenge on someone who broke your heart?
Answer: It was a Saturday in April, and the next morning I was to travel for work, but still she insisted on us attending this BBQ party organized by a member of her martial arts club. Because he would be there. She denied having feelings for this man — three weeks later, she would admit on the phone that she had been sleeping with him for months (apparently without any feelings whatsoever) — and I was the one who was imagining things. Stupid, selfish, paranoid me. Just a week before, I’d had a minor operation (some facial nevi — atypical and typically noncancerous moles — had to be removed), and so I looked like the elephant man — bandages and all. But I didn’t care anymore. The bandages hid more scars than anyone attending could ever imagine — they also hid the tears. And then there was the moment. During a tenth of a second, I clearly saw her touching his belly with a finger ever so briefly while she was dancing on an improvised dance floor, while looking into his eyes with a clear unspoken promise. And when she noticed that I had witnessed what she had done, she was startled and did not know how to behave. But she was caught — the elephant man had finally caught her in the act. And when I stood there in the garden of people almost unknown to me, bandaged and much more wounded than what showed, I could hardly stop more tears from flowing. But she had touched him, and that single anomaly said more to me than her thousand lies. And she knew it. At that moment, I realized that the next day I would travel abroad as a married man, but that all this would change soon after. She would not be there when I would come back, I would be erased from her past, and nothing could prevent us from sinking to depths which even in my darkest nightmares could not be reached. It was the very last time I would physically see her before our marriage would finally implode into the sad rotten truth a broken marriage afterwards becomes, and I knew deep inside that “we” were over and done with. And everyone was laughing, drinking, dancing, having fun. But I could hardly breathe. What is the best way to get revenge on someone who broke your heart ? To keep breathing. Even when it gets darker than every shade of dark you have ever experienced, even when it gets so cold that the breathing hurts, even when it gets so deep that standing up won’t help you anymore. Even when the horizons seem so very far. Because they are closer than you think. And if your heart breaks for the wrong reason, it might heal for the very right one. (Exhale.) SOURCES: painting by Hermen Anglada Camarasa (Salomé, c.1899).
